draft.title: Photosynthesis and respiration
card: Plants use light energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen. The light energy is stored as chemical energy in the glucose.
Cells oxidise glucose with oxygen to make carbon dioxide and water. This releases the stored energy for the cell to use.
The two processes run in opposite directions. The products of one are the reactants of the other.
Photosynthesis takes in energy from light. Respiration releases energy from glucose.
draft.remember: Photosynthesis stores light energy in glucose. Respiration releases it by turning glucose back into carbon dioxide and water.

a.q: Which pair of reactants is used in photosynthesis?
a.why: Photosynthesis builds glucose from carbon dioxide and water, using light energy. Glucose and oxygen are the reactants of respiration, which is the tempting wrong choice.
a.clue: Photosynthesis makes glucose, so glucose cannot be a reactant.

b.q: Priya's muscle cells release energy during a sprint. Which change is happening in them?
opts: Glucose is oxidised to carbon dioxide and water
Glucose is made from carbon dioxide and water
Light energy is stored as chemical energy
Carbon dioxide is used up and oxygen is made
b.why: Muscle cells release the energy stored in glucose by oxidising it to carbon dioxide and water, which is respiration. The other options describe photosynthesis, which is the reverse process and needs light.
b.clue: Releasing stored energy is the reverse of storing it.

b.best: Glucose is oxidised to carbon dioxide and water
